annotation.title_clean: The Legal Challenge of Robotic Assistance
annotation.title_en: The Legal Challenge of Robotic Assistance
annotation.venue: Robots in Care and Everyday Life, SpringerBriefs in Sociology (Springer)
named_instruments_referenced: EU Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI
annotation.summary_en: Book chapter analysing, under German law with EU context, legal challenges of consumer and care robots: liability, robot legal personhood, data protection, a right to human contact and discrimination. It argues existing abstract law (contract, tort, product liability) largely suffices, with new rules needed only where gaps appear, informed by a Delphi study.
key_provisions_or_claims: Existing abstract law (contract, tort, negligence) can largely regulate robots, which are legal objects.
Producer liability under the German Product Liability Act (Directive 85/374/EEC) covers robot-caused damage.
Joint and several liability applies among multiple injuring parties.
Focus on consumer and domestic robots because of consumer vulnerability and sensitive data.
Robots defined per ISO 8373 as machines performing movements via electronic control.
